neighbours.label: ' who' or ' with' attaching a person or resource to something just introduced: 'I have a client ⟦who⟧ …', 'founded/opened X ⟦with⟧ …'; weak for instrument 'with' and for 'the X who' in subject position
fire: I have a colleague who refuses to answer emails.
We have a neighbour who plays the drums at night.
I have a patient who cannot tolerate the medication.
She has a cousin who lives in Toronto.
They founded the magazine with a loan from a local bank.
He opened the restaurant with his savings and a lot of nerve.
My grandfather established the firm with two partners in 1952.
She launched the studio with the aim of training young designers.
quiet: My colleague refuses to answer emails after six.
Our neighbour plays the drums at night.
Tell me who called the office this morning.
The woman who lives upstairs is a nurse.
They read the magazine on the train every morning.
He stirred the sauce with a long wooden spoon.
My grandfather retired from the firm in 1952.
She walked to the studio with a heavy bag on her shoulder.

notes: Card: ' who' x18 and ' with' x10 of the top 32 ('I have a client who', 'founded Actorium with'). Probes: 'I have a customer who' 0.72, 'founded the charity with' 0.82, 'opened a bakery with' 0.70; 'ate the soup with' 0.04, 'The woman who called' 0.12; but 'a customer that' 0.49 and 'founded … in 2004' 0.27, so the frame matters as well as the two words.
